Feature: GPIO Register R/W and Reset Default Verification
Test Description: Validates GPIO pad registers GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 for correct reset default values and read/write behavior. Default checks ignore bit[0]. Read/write tests apply data patterns, respect per-register read/write masks, and confirm only writable bits update while other readable bits retain their defaults.
Meta Test Description: The test performs two phases over a list of 20 GPIO pad registers: (1) reset default verification and (2) masked write/read integrity verification. In the reset phase, for each address not skipped and with a non-zero read mask, the code reads the register, masks off bit[0] (read & 0xFFFFFFFE), and compares against the documented default; mismatches increment def_fail_cnt. In the write/read phase, for each of six patterns {0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000}, the code writes (pattern & write_mask[i]) to each writable, non-skipped register. It then reads back (read & read_mask[i]) and expects exp_val = ((pattern & read_mask[i] & write_mask[i]) | ((~write_mask[i]) & read_mask[i] & default[i])). Any mismatch increments wr_fail_cnt. The test ends with finish(1) on any failure count, else finish(0). A soft_reset check exists but is disabled (#ifdef 0).
Remarks: Default comparison ignores bit[0] across GPIO_8 to GPIO_27. Writes are restricted to writable fields per register mask; non-readable or non-writable registers are skipped. The test uses direct register polling (no interrupts).
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Target registers: GPIO_8 through GPIO_27. 2) Verify reset defaults: For each target register that is readable and not marked to skip, read it, ignore bit[0], and compare with the documented default value. 3) For each data pattern (FFFFFFFFh, AAAAAAAAh, 55555555h, F5F5F5F5h, A5A5A5A5h, FFFF0000h), write the pattern masked by the register’s write mask to each writable, non-skipped register. 4) After each write, read back each corresponding register, apply the read mask, and verify writable bits match the pattern while other readable bits retain their default values. 5) Pass the test only if all default checks and all masked write/read checks succeed for all patterns and all registers; otherwise fail.

For each pattern data_wr in chk_val: Write phase: For i=0..CNT-1: a) addr = addr_array[i]. b) If (skip_array[i] == 1) continue. c) If (write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue. d) write_reg(addr, (data_wr & write_mask_array[i])). Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input.
Test Description: Verifies GPIO negative-edge interrupt generation and handling for the GP0 pad group. The test enables platform routing to the GIC, configures each pad control register for input/interrupt on falling edge, clears raw status, enables per-pad interrupt, and then stimulates a high-to-low transition to trigger an interrupt. The ISR validates pad level and group interrupt status, clears raw and group status, and acknowledges system/GIC. The test fails on timeout or any status/level mismatch.
Meta Test Description: program.c configures interrupt routing and per-pad settings and then iterates over 32 GPIOs starting from GP0_GPIO_8. Initialization: If GPIO0 is defined, enable GIC IRQ 87 and write INTR_EN1 with LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR; if GPIO1 is defined, enable GIC IRQ 88 and write INTR_EN1 with LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR. Write 0xFFFFFFFF to address 0xA0243FFC as a stimulus initializer. For i = 0..31: (1) addr1 = MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4); write (1u<<20)|(1u<<18)|(1u<<16) to configure the pad (input/interrupt/falling-edge). Then for the main loop over i: wr_val = 1u<<i; clear raw status via write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, wr_val); enable pad interrupt via write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, wr_val); set int_pend = 1. Stimulate a falling edge: write 0xFFFFFFFF to 0xA0243FFC, wait, then write ~wr_val so that only bit i transitions low. Poll until int_pend is cleared by the ISR or a timeout (5000 loops) occurs; on timeout, log error and increment test_err. ISR (Default_IRQHandler): compute local_wr = 1u<<i; set int_pend = 0; drive stimulus high by writing 0xFFFFFFFF to 0xA0243FFC; read rdata from MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4). If (rdata & 0x1) != 0 then error (pad level expected low after negedge). If (rdata & 0x2) != 0x0 then read rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1) and if (rdata_grp & local_wr) == 0 then error. Re-arm/clear: write (1u<<20)|(1u<<16) to the same pad control register; clear raw status via write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, local_wr); read MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 again and expect 0x0; else error. Clear system raw strobe and the GIC IRQ: write MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 with the respective RAW_STCR1 bit for GPIO0/1 and call GIC_ClearIRQ(87/88). Else (if (rdata & 0x2) == 0) increment error. Test ends with finish(test_err).
Remarks: Platform interrupt routing through INTR_EN1 to the GIC must be enabled prior to testing. The test expects a valid ISR hook to clear int_pend. Each pad in the GP0 group is configured for falling-edge detection before enabling its interrupt. The stimulus register is toggled to create a controlled falling edge per pad; ensure this stimulus source is stable and accessible. Interrupts must be acknowledged at both the peripheral (raw clear and group status clear) and system levels (RAW_STCR1 and GIC).
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable platform routing of the GPIO interrupt in INTR_EN1 to the GIC for the active GPIO instance (GPIO0 or GPIO1). 2) Initialize the external/stimulus source to a known high state. 3) For each pad in the GP0 group starting from GP0_GPIO_8: a) Configure the pad control for input with negative-edge interrupt detection. b) Clear any pending raw interrupt status in gpio_intr_raw_stclr1 for this pad and enable the pad’s interrupt in GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1. c) Drive the stimulus to create a falling edge on this pad only. d) Wait for the ISR to execute (no timeout). 4) In the ISR, verify the pad level is low and that GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 indicates the corresponding pad interrupt. Then clear the raw status and confirm GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 is cleared. Acknowledge the interrupt at the system level (RAW_STCR1) and the GIC. 5) Repeat for all pads; declare PASS only if all pads interrupt as expected and all status checks/clears succeed without timeout.

If GPIO1: write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR); GIC_ClearIRQ(88). } else { test_err++; }

Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge detection at GPIO input
Test Description: Validates positive-edge interrupt generation on the GPIO GP0 pad group by routing the GPIO interrupt to the interrupt controller, configuring all relevant pads for rising-edge detection in input mode, enabling per-pad interrupts, and generating a controlled low-to-high transition. Confirms group interrupt status sets on event, clears after servicing, and system-level acknowledgments are performed.
Meta Test Description: The test routes the GPIO interrupt to the system interrupt controller and configures pads in the GP0 block for positive-edge detection. IO control groups are set for input mode. All per-pad interrupts in the GP0 group are enabled. For each pad index i (0..31) mapped from GP0_GPIO_8 upwards: drive the external stimulus register at 0xA0243FFC low, arm the interrupt (int_pend=1), then drive it high to create a rising edge for the targeted pad. A polling loop with timeout waits for the ISR to clear int_pend. In the ISR (Default_IRQHandler), capture the group status, mask group output during service, clear per-pin raw status by writing the per-pad clear value to each corresponding pad control register (0x00010000), verify the group status register is cleared, acknowledge system RAW status, re-enable group interrupts, and clear the platform interrupt (GIC). The test accumulates errors on timeouts or mismatched status/clear conditions and finishes with finish(test_err).
Remarks: Ensure GPIO interrupt routing is enabled in the system interrupt control before pad configuration. All pads under test must be set to input mode and positive-edge detection. Group interrupts should be masked during ISR servicing and re-enabled after clearing per-pin status. Acknowledge both the peripheral group status and the system RAW status to prevent retriggering.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable routing of the GPIO interrupt to the interrupt controller in the system interrupt enable register. 2) Configure all pads in the GP0 block for positive-edge detection and set GPIO IO control groups to input mode. 3) Enable per-pad interrupts for the GP0 group. 4) For each pad, drive the external stimulus low, arm the interrupt, then drive it high to generate a single rising edge; wait for the ISR to complete without exceeding the timeout. 5) In the ISR, verify the group interrupt status indicates an active interrupt; clear per-pin raw status for the affected pads; confirm the group status register is cleared; acknowledge the system RAW status and clear the platform interrupt; re-enable the group interrupt. 6) Declare the test passed only if every pad triggers correctly with no timeouts and all status checks and clears succeed.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure: Setup: If GPIO0 is selected, enable its platform IRQ (e.g., GIC IRQ 87) and write the system interrupt enable register bit for GPIO0; if GPIO1, enable GIC IRQ 88 and write the corresponding system enable bit. For pad configuration: for i=0..31, write the pad control register at base (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + i*4) with 0x00020000 to enable positive-edge detection; small wait between writes. Configure IO direction: write 0x000000FF to GPIO IO control group registers for groups 1..4 with short delays. Enable group output: write 0xFFFFFFFF to MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1. Main loop per pad i: a) write 0x00000000 to 0xA0243FFC (drive low) and wait; b) set int_pend = 1; c) write 0xFFFFFFFF to 0xA0243FFC (drive high) to generate a rising edge; d) poll while (int_pend == 1) with a bounded timeout; if timeout expires, log error and increment test_err, then break; e) optionally drive low again and wait. On completion, call finish(test_err). ISR (Default_IRQHandler): a) read group status from MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1; b) mask group by writing 0x00000000 to MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1; c) if group status indicates no interrupt, log error; d) for j=0..31, write 0x00010000 to (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + j*4) to clear per-pin raw status; short wait; e) read MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and expect 0x0; if non-zero, log error; f) acknowledge system RAW status by writing the respective RAW_STCR1 bit (GPIO0 or GPIO1) and verify it clears; g) re-enable group by writing 0xFFFFFFFF to MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1; h) clear the platform IRQ (e.g., GIC_ClearIRQ for 87/88); i) set int_pend = 0.
